title: WorldEnvironment in Canvas Mode affects distinct SubViewports
body:
### Tested versions

Tested version Godot 4.6.3.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.5.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon Pro 5300M OpenGL Engine - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9750H CPU @ 2.60GHz (12 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

Overview: when `WorldEnvironment` is enabled in one `SubViewport` it changes the alpha blending of another `SubViewport`.

Example set up:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c03987e-4add-4a6d-994a-e38c603c618f

World (CanvasLayer)
- SubViewportContainer1
  - SubViewport
    - ColorRect (50% opacity)
- SubViewportContainer2 (Material with premultiplied alpha blend mode)
  - SubViewport (transparent background)
    - ColorRect (50% opacity)

When configured like this, the two colour rects appear as the same colour. However, if we add `WorldEnvironment` to `SubViewportContainer1` as a child of `SubViewport1` in `CANVAS` mode with `glow` (or another effect) enabled

World (CanvasLayer)
- SubViewportContainer1
  - SubViewport1
    - ColorRect1 (50% opacity)
    - WorldEnvironment
- SubViewportContainer2 (Material with premultiplied alpha blend mode)
  - SubViewport2 (transparent background)
    - ColorRect2 (50% opacity)

`ColorRect2` now appears darker than `ColorRect1`

You can "fix" this by setting own world 3D on `SubViewport2`, but i don't know if this is fixing buggy behaviour or the intended process. It feels weird `WorldEnvironment` can effect the alpha blending of a distinct viewport.

### Steps to reproduce

```
CanvasLayer
- SubViewportContainer1
  - SubViewport1
    - ColorRect1 (50% opacity)
    - WorldEnvironment (Canvas mode, glow enabled)
- SubViewportContainer2 (Material with premultiplied alpha blend mode)
  - SubViewport2 (transparent background)
    - ColorRect2 (50% opacity)
```

`ColorRect2` now appears darker than `ColorRect1`

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[transparency-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28790157/transparency-bug.zip)
